inventory.producer: collectLocalScriptEntries(scriptsDir) at skills-conformance-check.ts:988-1003 — specifically the walk-global `visited` set keyed on resolvedRealPath(dir) (:997-999). It is the sole decider of whether a directory's entries are emitted AT ALL, and it drops whichever NAME of a doubly-named directory readdirSync yields SECOND. It, not compareInstalledTwin, therefore owns the class of a directory reachable under two names — and it owns BOTH names symmetrically, which is why the class is a cross-product and not a single case.
inputs: a dataset scripts/ tree holding a REAL sub-directory (scripts/zzz-lib/) and, beside it, a symlinked sub-directory that ALIASES it (scripts/<alias> -> scripts/zzz-lib) — an alias, NOT a cycle: the target is a sibling, not an ancestor

AXIS 1 — which name readdirSync yields FIRST, decided by the alias NAME (`aaa-alias` sorts before `zzz-lib`; `zzz9-alias` after, since `-` 0x2D < `9` 0x39). The name that arrives SECOND is the one dropped.

AXIS 2 — which installed twin has DRIFTED. BOTH names really ship (the directory is reachable under each, so `pair update` installs a twin at each mirrored path), so each side is independently guardable and each is an independent input.
the two axes are independent, so the class is the 2x2 they span — four cells, of which TWO are red at this head, one in each column
a TRUE cycle for contrast: scripts/lib/loop -> scripts (the target IS an ancestor of the descent)
representations: canonical dataset script bytes reached under EITHER name
the installed twin at EACH mirrored path (pair-workflow-alpha/scripts/zzz-lib/util.mjs AND pair-workflow-alpha/scripts/<alias>/util.mjs) — both ship, both are guarded
the RunResult.errors line (DRIFTED, naming both paths)
CLI exit code via runChecks / pnpm skills:conformance
classes: THE CLASS, stated once and in full: every name under which a directory really ships is compared against its own installed twin, whichever name readdirSync yields first. Both halves are answered — not the real half only. Concretely the 2x2 of {which name arrives first} x {which twin drifted}, all four cells asserted:

CELL 1 (alias-first, drift on the REAL twin) -> exactly one DRIFTED error naming workflow/alpha/scripts/zzz-lib/util.mjs (R30, WITNESS). At 9735d2da: 0 errors — the alias consumes the real directory's realpath in `visited` and the real arrival returns early, so a drifted shipped file is answered with silence.
CELL 2 (real-first, drift on the REAL twin) -> the same single DRIFTED error naming the same real path (R31, CONTROL). Already correct at 9735d2da.

CELL 3 (real-first, drift on the ALIAS twin) -> exactly one DRIFTED error naming workflow/alpha/scripts/zzz9-alias/util.mjs (R33, WITNESS). At 9735d2da: 0 errors — the mirror image of CELL 1 with the two names swapped, the same defect, and the cell revision 3 attempt 1 left unwatched.

CELL 4 (alias-first, drift on the ALIAS twin) -> exactly one DRIFTED error naming workflow/alpha/scripts/aaa-alias/util.mjs (R34, CONTROL). Already correct at 9735d2da, and it is the half a naive order-based fix silently trades away.

a TRUE cycle (scripts/lib/loop -> scripts, target an ancestor of the current descent) -> the walk terminates, does not throw, and still names the real nested script scripts/lib/util.mjs (R32). Termination alone is not the class: a fix may not buy it by abandoning the subtree.

real file / real sub-directory / symlinked file / symlinked non-aliasing sub-directory / dangling entry -> answers unchanged (R5, R7, R21, R22, R23, R24, R25, R28 — the regression boundary of this fix)
the real corpus, which holds ZERO symlinks -> unchanged, still clean (R14, R15)
interactions: THE CROSS-PRODUCT IS THE UNIT. Each column alone is under-determined: the {drift-on-real} pair (R30 red, R31 pass) proves only that the REAL half currently depends on readdir order; the {drift-on-alias} pair (R33 red, R34 pass) proves the same of the ALIAS half. Neither pair alone forbids a fix that satisfies its own column by dropping the other. Only all four cells together state the obligation — every shipped name is compared, in either order.

DISCRIMINANCE, proved not asserted. The candidate fix "order real directories before symlinked ones and keep the global `visited` set" satisfies the letter of the order-independence invariant and makes R30, R31 AND R32 pass, while turning CELL 4 from 1 error to 0 — a straight regression — and leaving CELL 3 at 0. Probed at 9735d2da against an isolated patched COPY of the module (no production edit): R30 PASS, R31 PASS, R32 PASS, R33 FAIL (0 hits), R34 FAIL (0 hits). Without R33 and R34 that fix passes the whole suite while the gate stays silent over half the shipped names; with them it cannot.

NO OVER-SPECIFICATION, proved on the same rig. The admissible ancestor-chain resolution (push/pop the resolved path of the CURRENT descent instead of a walk-global set) passes all five: R30, R31, R33, R34 each with exactly 1 hit, and R32 terminating without throwing and still naming scripts/lib/util.mjs. The second admissible resolution the finding names — keep a global set but still emit an already-visited subtree's entries under its second relative path — yields the identical entry list and therefore the identical answers. The rows assert the ANSWER at each mirrored path, never a walk strategy.

R30/R33 and R32 pull in opposite directions over the same three lines: the cheapest way to pass the witnesses is to delete the `visited` set, which makes R32's true cycle recurse until the stack dies and takes the whole gate down. R32 is the trap the witnesses set, exactly as R28 is the trap R23/R24 set — and it is why the fix must distinguish an ANCESTOR (a cycle: bound it) from a SIBLING (an alias: walk it, or emit its entries under the second relative path too).

the corpus cannot discriminate any of this: 10 flat scripts, zero symlinks, zero sub-directories at this head (re-derived below), so R14/R15 stay green under the defect, under the bad candidate and under either admissible fix.
